title: Asking who pays him: learning the band had a manager
summary: After sending home for money, Johnny Hodges told him to ask manager Al Celley; Procope was used to asking the leader himself.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: had any money since you've been here?" I said no. And all the fellows looked at me, you know, wondering how am I getting along. They didn't know that I'd sent home to my wife for some money in the meantime. So when I sent it -- when I sent home for the money, Johnny Hodges knew I'd -- you know, because I think he knew I'd gone to Western Union or something. So Johnny called me aside. He said, "Now, you didn't have to do that. You didn't have to send home for money." I said, "Well, I didn't know the ropes, you know." Then I found out this guy sitting up front with the glasses was the manager. Al Colley Sully, you know.
He's the guy you're supposed to ask for money. You know, I didn't know. I'm used to working for a man, if I'm working --
No-one told me, right. You know, if you're working for Jim Jones you ask Jim Jones for the money. But this is big time. He had a manager.
